question: A person invested ₹20,000 in two different schemes. He invested one part for 4 years at 8% simple interest and the other part for the same duration at 10% simple interest. If the interest earned from the second part was ₹2,240 more than the interest earned from the first part, how much money was invested in the second scheme?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest rates for 4 years: Scheme 1 = 32%, Scheme 2 = 40%

Let Scheme 2 investment be x, then Scheme 1 investment is (20000 − x).

40% of x − 32% of (20000 − x) = 2240

72% of x − 6400 = 2240 ⇒ x = 8640 ÷ 0.72 = 12000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Investment = ₹20,000

Scheme 1: Rate (R₁) = 8%, Time (T) = 4 years

Scheme 2: Rate (R₂) = 10%, Time (T) = 4 years

Difference in Interest (I₂ − I₁) = ₹2,240

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
